headlines.text: It was 2023 when FTR vs. Bullet Club Gold clashed for the AEW World Tag Team Titles in a 2 out of 3 Falls match, appearing on Collision, rated 9.47 ? an all-time classic. For Bullet Club Gold, it marked a first real shot at championship gold. In a near hour-long instant classic filled with tributes to the Hart family in their hometown of Calgary, FTR outlasted Bullet Club Gold in a 2-out-of-3 falls match to retain the tag titles.

It was 2026 when Kyle Fletcher vs. Komander put the AEW International Title on the line, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.17 ? an excellent showing. In his first defense as champion, Fletcher survived a Rope Walk Dive and a 450 splash from Komander before cutting off a Tornado DDT attempt mid-rotation with a Sheer Drop Brainbuster to retain the International Championship.

Flash back to 2020, when Cody vs. Sonny Kiss clashed for the AEW TNT Title, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.21. For Sonny Kiss, it marked a first real shot at championship gold. Championship gold always raises the stakes.

secondaries.text: 2022 brought us this moment: Alex Reynolds returned to the fold after just under 4 months away, appearing on Rampage.

Back on this day in 2022, Jonathan Gresham vs. Lee Moriarty went to battle over the ROH World Heavyweight Title, appearing on Rampage, rated 6.74. For Lee Moriarty, it marked a first real shot at championship gold.

That Wednesday in 2020, the AEW World Heavyweight Title was up for grabs as Jon Moxley vs. Brian Cage went to war, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.80. For Brian Cage, it marked a first real shot at championship gold.
